subject: SOC 2 Type II: audit-window endpoints and snapshot mapping for Finex Health
messages:
From: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@liaisonaudit.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification on SOC 2 Type II period endpoints for Finex Health

Hi Vanessa,

Quick question from the audit team as we prepare testing: can you confirm how Redwood defines the end-of-period timestamp for SOC 2 Type II evidence? Specifically: is the audit period end_date inclusive through 23:59:59 UTC on the final day, or do you treat daily snapshots (taken at 00:00) as the canonical point-in-time capture for the previous day?

We have a scenario where Finex Health generates events between 00:00 and 02:00 UTC on the first day after the audit period — for example, a timezone-shifted on-prem gateway writes logs stamped in Finex's local time that precede midnight local time. For our testing we need to know whether those events are considered part of the audit period (i.e., counted in point-in-time evidence) or are treated as after the period cutoff.

If you have a standard approach or a bridge letter we can rely on, that would be helpful. Also: what evidence artifacts can you share to demonstrate the capture method (snapshot manifest, log extracts with timezone stamps, or a signed bridge letter)?

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Meyers
Senior Associate, Liaison Audit LLP

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@liaisonaudit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SOC 2 Type II period endpoints for Finex Health

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear note. Short answer: we treat the audit period end as inclusive of the final calendar day, and our standard evidence model uses point-in-time snapshots that we take at 00:00 UTC (manifested as the snapshot for the prior day). That means that: 

- The "snapshot" captured at 00:00 UTC is considered the canonical capture for the previous day.
- Events that are generated after 00:00 UTC are not included in that previous-day snapshot unless they were ingested earlier and backfilled into that snapshot window.

Where it gets nuanced (and I suspect is the source of your example) is systems that emit logs with local timestamps that are earlier than 00:00 UTC. In practice we rely on ingestion timestamps (UTC) for audit evidence, but we can provide two complementary artifacts to make this auditable:

1) Snapshot manifest (attached) that lists the snapshot timestamp and sequence IDs for files included in each daily capture (snapshot-manifest.csv).
2) Sample log extracts (attached) showing both the original event timestamp and our ingestion timestamp (sample-log-extract.csv).

If the auditor prefers, we can also provide one of two options:
- A signed bridge letter that documents our snapshot policy and confirms that snapshots at 00:00 UTC are used as the point-in-time evidence for the prior day (we can include language about reliance on ingestion timestamps).
- Raw ingestion logs for a short sample window (we normally redact sensitive fields) so you can validate specific events.

Which option would you like us to pursue? If you want a bridge letter, we can circulate a draft for review and arrange signature through DocuSign. Happy to hop on a quick call if that helps.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference

Attachments: snapshot-manifest.csv (stub), sample-log-extract.csv (stub)

From: Emily Cho <emily.cho@finexhealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, jordan.meyers@liaisonaudit.com
Date: 2026-10-14T11:20:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SOC 2 Type II period endpoints for Finex Health

Thanks Vanessa & Jordan — appreciate the quick turn. A couple follow-ups from Finex's compliance team: 

- Can you confirm whether events generated between 00:00 and 02:00 UTC (but stamped in Finex local time as occurring before midnight local) would ever be backfilled into the 00:00 UTC snapshot, or are those always excluded? We need an explicit statement for our auditor that local-timestamped events cannot be re-assigned to the prior day's snapshot unless there is evidence of backfill.

- If Redwood is able to provide a bridge letter, can you include the exact wording that will be used about ingestion timestamps vs. original event timestamps? Finex's auditors require a signed bridge letter attached to the SOC 2 package (preferably as a PDF or DocuSign).

- Also please confirm which SOC 2 Type II report you will attach: the latest period we requested ends on 2026-09-30. If you could specify the report cover dates and the bridge-letter signatory, we can circulate internally.

Thanks,
Emily Cho
Compliance Manager, Finex Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Cho <emily.cho@finexhealth.com>, Jordan Meyers <jordan.meyers@liaisonaudit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-14T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification on SOC 2 Type II period endpoints for Finex Health

Emily — understood. To be explicit:

- Our operational rule: snapshots taken at 00:00 UTC are the point-in-time evidence for the prior calendar day; we do not retroactively reassign events to a prior-day snapshot unless we have a documented backfill process (rare, and we would supply change logs). Ingestion timestamp (UTC) is the authoritative field we use for audit captures.

- We will provide a signed bridge letter that includes the following language (draft attached): "Redwood Inference uses 00:00 UTC daily snapshots as the point-in-time evidence for the prior calendar day. Evidence is indexed by ingestion timestamp (UTC). Events ingested after the snapshot time are not included in that snapshot unless they were backfilled and documented."

- The SOC 2 Type II report we will attach covers the period 2026-04-01 through 2026-09-30 (Type II). The bridge letter will be signed by Marissa Cole (Head of Security Compliance).

Next steps: 
1) Please review the attached draft-bridge-letter.pdf and the evidence-manifest.xlsx.
2) If the language looks good, we'll route the bridge letter for signature via DocuSign (link will be shared).
3) Upon signature, we will deliver the unredacted sample logs for your auditors under an access-controlled link.

If you'd like a short call to finalize wording, Ben and I are available tomorrow morning PST.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Compliance & Trust
Redwood Inference
